code_licence: GPL v3 (LICENSE at repo root; forge-gui/LICENSE.txt). README calls it an open-source Rules Engine for Magic: The Gathering. Bundled libraries carry their own licences in forge-gui/res/licenses (multiline-label, tinylog, xpp3, xstream).
asset_licence: Mixed by group, per the repo's own credit files. Kevin MacLeod music: CC BY 3.0 (forge-gui/res/music/Credit.txt). Particle Park effects: CC BY 4.0 (particle_effects/Particle Park License.txt). Dock-bar icons: CC BY 3.0 per docs/Credit-and-Thanks.md. Adventure sprites and tiles: each artist's own licence, which is not in the repo. Other music, sound effects, fonts and skins: no licence line in the repo. Card art is not in the repo; the FAQ points to in-app downloaders.
rights_holder_status: mixed and partly unknown. Fan/community open-source rules engine for Magic: The Gathering; README and forge-installer/ReadMeForge.txt both say it is not related to or affiliated with Wizards of the Coast. Card names and card rules scripts are in the repo with no ownership statement. Adventure sprites credited to individual artists, one credited to a Reddit user for 'iconic MTG characters'. Rights to those characters are not stated in the repo.

inspiration: Colour-family hero sprites: the dragonplayer sheets come in five suffixed variants (b, g, r, u, w). One silhouette, five palette swaps, each in a 16 px frame with nearest-neighbour filtering. A clear way to give each faction its own look without redrawing the figure.

Creature families in separate folders (undead, fiend, monstrosity, elemental, humanoid), each with a sheet and a text atlas. A tidy bestiary structure: a family sets the silhouette rules, and a single creature is one more row in the atlas.

Particle library organised as short bursts and trails (blood, fireball, burnout, pentagram, rain, smoke trail, starlight). Recreate the timing and the burst-plus-trail pairing with our own palette and sprite shapes.
Compact town and cave maps: 30x17-tile rooms at 16 px, with named encounter maps per region (cave, evilgrove, merfolkpool, towns). A simple room grammar that keeps each encounter small.
One full-screen backdrop per biome (cave, swamp, waste, island, castle, forest) behind menus and encounters, drawn in a low-saturation palette. A cheap way to tell the player where they are.
Effects are separate .p emitter files (bursts, trails, glows) layered over sprites, so one sprite can get a burst or a glow without new frames.
Sprite sheets are small and fixed-grid (16 px frames in atlas rows), which keeps the animation work manageable for one artist.
